title: Ex 3.2 #7(b) · 4-letter codes, no letter twice in a row
prompt: A code is a list of 4 letters from A to Z, and letters may repeat. How many codes have no two consecutive letters the same? For example, ABAB is allowed but ABBC is not.
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: That forbids any letter from appearing twice anywhere. Only consecutive letters must differ: a letter may come back later, as in ABAB.
That counts every 4-letter code, including ones like AABC with two equal letters side by side.

hints: Fill the code from left to right. How many choices are there for the first letter?
Each later letter only has to differ from the letter just before it.
solution: The first letter can be any of the 26. Each of the next three letters must differ from the letter just before it, which leaves 25 choices each time.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the multiplication principle (Section 3.2).
